Subject: Private deployment — SSO & SCIM requirements (control plane)

Hi Mateo,

Thanks for taking this on. We're starting the security and procurement review for the on-prem Redwood Private deployment and need to confirm how the control plane will integrate with our identity stack. High-level requirements from our InfoSec and IT teams: 

- SAML 2.0 support (SP-initiated and IdP-initiated preferred), metadata exchange and cert rotation process.
- SCIM 2.0 provisioning: create/update/delete users and groups, group-to-role sync.
- Fine-grained role mapping: we need mapping from our AD groups to Redwood roles (admin, deployer, observer), and a way to support custom roles in the future.
- Audit logs showing identity events (user provisioning, role changes) with at least 365 days retention for now.
- Ability to rotate SCIM tokens/credentials without service interruption.
- TLS mutual auth for on-prem SCIM endpoint would be a plus.

We have a compliance audit scheduled for 2026-09-15 and would like a mutual action plan to get SSO/SCIM verified by 2026-09-01. Can you share a recommended mapping template, your preferred SCIM auth model, and any network prerequisites (IP allowlist, peering/VPN expectations) for private control plane access?

Also copying Marcus and Monica from Redmond — Marcus will be our infra contact and Monica will coordinate contract addenda.

Thanks,

Laura Sweeney
Head of IT Security — Acme Financial

Hi Laura — great summary, thanks. 

Below is a concise plan and the defaults we recommend for Redwood Private control plane identity integration. I've attached a short integration PDF and a YAML example for group->role mapping.

Key points:
- SAML: we support SAML 2.0, both SP-initiated and IdP-initiated. We exchange metadata (XML) and use RSA-SHA256 for signature algorithms by default. Cert rotation is handled by exchanging new metadata and can be coordinated with zero-downtime if the new cert appears in metadata at least 48 hours prior to expiry.

- SCIM: Redwood exposes a SCIM 2.0 endpoint for provisioning. Auth model: bearer token issued per-customer; token rotation is supported via a short overlap window (create new token, update customer config, revoke old token). We support TLS and can require client certs for mutual TLS on private deployments.

- Role mapping: default roles: Admin, Deployer, Observer. Group-to-role sync is handled by SCIM groupToRole mapping; see attached sso-mapping-example.yaml for syntax (we can support nested groups via group claims if your IdP provides them). For custom roles we'll accept an onboarding mapping file and add a mapping record in the control plane.

- Audit logs: identity events (SCIM create/update/delete, SAML auth events, role changes) are logged and available via the console and API. For Private, we can ship logs to your SIEM (syslog/forwarding) or retain them in the control plane for 365+ days depending on contract.

- Networking: control plane needs to reach your IdP metadata URL and SCIM endpoint (for customer-hosted SCIM). For Redwood-hosted SCIM you only need to allow outbound TLS to our control plane IPs; for customer-hosted SCIM we require inbound connectivity from our control plane to your SCIM endpoint — typical options are site-to-site VPN or VPC peering. We will provide a CIDR/IP allowlist and recommended port list (443 + mTLS ports if used).

Next steps / owners:
1) Mateo (me) to share the integration checklist + mapping example (attached) — target 2026-08-06.
2) Acme (Laura S.) to provide IdP metadata and group naming conventions — target 2026-08-10.
3) Marcus (Acme infra) and our infra team to schedule a short network connectivity test (VPN/peering) — target 2026-08-14.
4) Monica & Laura B. to draft control plane identity addendum for legal/compliance sign-off — target 2026-08-12.

If helpful, we can run a 30-min technical call this week to walk through the mapping YAML and SCIM auth flow.

Best,

Quick clarifying items from our side: 

- IdP-initiated vs SP-initiated: do you require both? If Acme is okay with SP-initiated only for the initial rollout, that simplifies testing.
- Cert rotation: we recommend a documented overlap window (48h) and an emergency rotation playbook. Laura S., can your IdP support publishing metadata with both certs present?
- SCIM token rotation cadence: do you need automatic rotation every X days or manual rotation with API? We typically suggest 90 days but are flexible.
- JIT provisioning: any need for Just-in-Time provisioning for ad-hoc contractors? If yes, we need to design a deprovisioning TTL.
- Network: Marcus, can you confirm if Acme will do site-to-site VPN or expose a peered VPC? We need an expected contact for network testing.

I'll start a draft addendum and upload to Drive — looping in Laura B. for legal wording.

—Monica
